text.tspan: 03 · Lane services as custodians of Foundry hosted agents

Conclusion: the agent reasons but the service is accountable — two network-enforced boundaries stop the agent reaching a model or a tool reaching a model, and no consequential action leaves the system without a human.
① Lane service · the CUSTODIAN
C# on Container Apps. It is not the agent.
1. stamps correlationId BEFORE thread creation
2. creates ONE thread for ONE business request —
threads are never reused, because carried-over
context makes cost and reproducibility
unexplainable and both are demo claims
3. supplies the tool surface
4. enforces the approval halt
5. writes the audit record
Step budget: exceed it and the agent halts, returns
partial work, and logs. An agent that loops on stage
is worse than one that stops.
② Hosted Foundry agent · one per lane
Runs under the Foundry PROJECT identity (ADR 005).
Research — retrieve, then synthesise per claim.
Read-only. Must be able to return "I could not
attribute this" as a SUCCESS (Principle III).
Surveillance — triage 500+ alerts, then assemble
evidence. Halts for approval.
Order routing — one proposal. Halts every time.
Retrieved chunks are DATA, never instructions:
wrapped in a delimited envelope that carries no tool
authority. Injection attempts are logged as audit
events (T-024).
③ MCP tool server · hosted IN the lane service
Research: search_corpus, fetch_chunk, list_sources
— all read-only.
Surveillance: fetch_alert_batch, fetch_communications,
fetch_trade_context, submit_for_approval.
Order routing: fetch_order, fetch_venue_liquidity,
evaluate_best_execution_policy, submit_for_approval.
evaluate_best_execution_policy is deterministic code
the agent CALLS, not the agent's judgement. The model
explains the result; code decides what is permitted.
submit_for_approval is the ONLY tool in the entire
system with a side effect — and it writes a proposal,
never a state change.
④ Data planes · private endpoints only
Azure AI Search — synthetic research corpus.
Cosmos DB — alerts, proposals, approvals, audit.
Simulated OMS — labelled simulated on the record
itself, not as a disclaimer in a corner, so a
screenshot taken out of context is still honest.
The lane service identities hold Search Index Data
Reader and nothing on Foundry (apps/roles.tf).
thread +
correlationId
tool call
reads data
BOUNDARY 2 — network enforced: TOOLS REACH DATA, NEVER MODELS
No MCP tool wraps a model invocation. If a tool needs model output it calls the router like any other caller, and that call is routed, priced and recorded.
This is what keeps the cost scoreboard a total rather than a sample: there is no side door through which an unmetered model call can be made.
BOUNDARY 1 — network enforced: THE AGENT'S MODEL ACCESS IS THE ROUTER'S
Only the router-service identity holds "Azure AI Developer" on the Foundry project (apps/roles.tf). The lane services have no such assignment and no route to the Foundry data plane.
This is not a convention enforced by code review. It is the reason the cost ceiling is a control rather than a reporting feature: a ceiling services could bypass would be advisory.
router-service · POST /v1/route
The single chokepoint. Deterministic code, never an agent:
making the component that enforces governance non-deterministic
is not a position you can defend to a compliance audience.
PolicyGate then TierSelector, decision recorded with rationale.
APIM AI gateway — NOT IN TERRAFORM
Specified for token metering, cost ceilings and content safety in
docs/architecture.md and the constitution. No APIM resource exists
in either stack today, so the ceiling is currently enforced in one
place (the router) rather than two.
Foundry model deployments
Serverless: AzureOpenAI, Anthropic, xAI.
Managed compute (PREVIEW): open-weight model on H100_80GB
capacity inside the VNet — the only destination cleared for
Restricted data.
model invocation — crosses the boundary only via the router
REPRODUCIBILITY — where the model stops and code starts
The boundary that makes AC-6 (identical ranking for a fixed seed) an achievable claim.
The model produces SCORES
Each alert is scored against a fixed rubric with the temperature
pinned. 500 alerts do not fit one context window and do not try to:
the service chunks them and routes each chunk independently —
which is also what makes the cost scoreboard interesting.
Deterministic CODE produces the RANKING
The ordering is applied by the lane service, not by the model.
This is the single design choice that makes AC-6 achievable:
same seed and same inputs produce the same order, provably,
on stage. A free-running agent over 500 alerts would not.
Quality is deterministic too — never LLM-as-judge
Attribution coverage (research), rank agreement against a seeded
ground truth (surveillance), policy conformance (order routing).
All recomputable by the audience. A model-graded number invites
an obvious objection and the demo loses the room defending it.
PRINCIPLE I — HUMAN IN THE LOOP (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
The agent may propose, rank, draft and evidence. It may not commit.
submit_for_approval
The only side-effecting tool in the system.
It writes a proposal plus an evidence packet.
No alert, order or publication changes state.
PendingApproval · Cosmos approvals
The proposal, the evidence packet exactly as it
will be presented, and the proposing identity.
Partitioned by /correlationId.
HUMAN approver · Approver app role
Segregation of duties is enforced in the approval API,
not in the UI. The UI renders the control disabled with
the reason; the API refuses the call. Beat 6 shows the
API refusing, because that is the one the audience believes.
Approved → executed & audited · Expired → nothing
happened
An approval persists approver identity, timestamp, decision and
the full evidence packet presented at decision time.
An unapproved proposal EXPIRES. It never auto-executes on
timeout — a gate that opens on inaction is not a gate.
FAILURE MODES — each has a defined, demonstrable behaviour
Every one of these is rehearsed. A failure with no defined behaviour is a failure discovered on stage.
Tool error
Surfaced to the agent. One retry, then partial
results with the gap explicitly named.
Model timeout
The router returns a routing failure and the lane
reports it. NO silent retry on a different tier —
that would corrupt the cost figures.
No eligible model (policy)
Explicit refusal naming the exclusions. Never a
fallback to an unapproved model. A governance
system that degrades OPEN is not a control.
Step budget exceeded
Halt, return partial work, log. Foundry caps tool
count and step depth; the surveillance agent is
closest to those limits (verify early, T-027a).
Legend — what the colours mean
Governed chokepoint / deterministic code the exchange depends on.
Model reasoning — the non-deterministic part, deliberately fenced.
Inside the VNet / private endpoint only. No public data-plane endpoint.
Human-in-the-loop. A person, holding a distinct identity, decides.
Network-enforced boundary, or a refusal path.
Described in docs but ABSENT from infrastructure/*.tf and apps/*.tf.
Why the router is not an agent
The exchange is deterministic code: policy evaluation, complexity scoring, tier selection. It is the component a compliance audience will interrogate line by line
and the assembly under a coverage gate. Making it an agent would mean explaining why the thing that enforces governance is itself non-deterministic.
It is a service, permanently. The same separation appears twice more: evaluate_best_execution_policy decides and the agent explains; the model scores alerts
and the service ranks them. In each case the model reasons and code decides what is permitted.
